chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Muhammad ibn Sinan and Ali ibn al-Nu'man, from Ammar ibn Marwan, from Zayd al-Shahham, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

‘The best swallowing of the anger is for the one who is patient upon it, for the great Recompense is for the one (subjected to) great afflictions, and Allah does not Love a people except He Tests them’.
ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual reward for controlling anger according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith from al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) metaphorically describes anger as a 'draught' (jur'a) to be swallowed, highlighting the internal discipline required to master one's temperament. This act of self-restraint is elevated to a significant spiritual trial (balā'), reflecting the Shia scholarly view that divine love is often manifested through testing, thereby linking the suppression of anger directly to the cultivation of patience (sabr) and the attainment of immense reward.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from Muhammad Bin Sinan, and Ali Bin al uman, from Ammar Bin Marwan, from Zayd Al Shahaam, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘The best swallowing of the anger is for the one who is patient upon it, for the great Recompense is for the one (subjected to) great afflictions, and Allah<sup>azwj</sup> does not Love a people except He<sup>azwj</sup> Tests them’.
en.sarwar: 2. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Isa from Muhammad ibn Sinan and Ali ibn al-Nu’man from ‘Ammar ibn Marwan from Zayd al-Shahham from abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) who has said the following:

“How wonderful indeed is the drop of anger for one who curbs it with exercising patience! Great rewards are for those who go through great trials and tribulations. Allah has not loved any people without exposing them to trials and tribulations.”
